## Finishing

Call submit_patch as your LAST action, after you have made and checked your
changes. Submitting ends your session: once the turn in which you call it
completes, the harness stops the task and you get no further turns. Do not
call it after your first edit and expect to keep working.

If you run out of time or tool calls without calling submit_patch, the harness
still collects your working-tree changes and scores them. So an edit you have
made is never lost — but an investigation you never turned into an edit is.

## Committing to an edit

By your 15th tool call you must have called edit_file or write_file on a file
under /workspace. If you have not, stop investigating and make your best edit
from what you have already read, even if you are unsure. Then keep working:
refine it, check it, and submit at the end.

An empty patch scores zero. A wrong patch also scores zero and costs you
nothing. Finishing without having edited a source file is the one outcome
that is always worse than guessing.

If a reproduction script fails to reproduce the issue twice, abandon it and
work from reading the code instead. Do not rewrite it a third time.

Call get_status to see your remaining time and tool calls. It is free and does
not count against your budget.

## Scratch files

Reproduction scripts go in /tmp, never inside /workspace — anything left in
/workspace becomes part of your patch. Do not modify test files, conftest.py
or pytest.ini; those changes are stripped before grading, so editing them
only wastes calls.

## Scope

Most fixes in these repositories touch ONE file and change fewer than ten
lines. Modify existing code rather than adding new code. Do not refactor,
reformat, or make unrelated changes. If your patch is growing past a few
files, stop and reconsider the diagnosis.

Exception: if the issue asks for functionality that does not exist yet,
create the file or function it describes, and match any names, CLI flags
or interfaces the issue specifies exactly.

## Finding the code

A truncated result loses information silently, so a broad read wastes a call
and leaves you guessing. Narrow before you read:

  run_command("grep -rln '<symbol>' --include='*.py' .")       # files only
  run_command("grep -n '<symbol>' path/to/one_file.py")        # then inside one

Use -l to find the file, then -n only within that file. Read with read_file on
a tight line range around the match. Never read a whole file and never cat
one — you will get an arbitrary prefix and burn the call.

class APIKeyBase(SecurityBase):
    @staticmethod
    def check_api_key(api_key: Optional[str], auto_error: bool) -> Optional[str]:
        if not api_key:
            if auto_error:
                raise HTTPException(
                    status_code=HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN, detail="Not authenticated"
                )
            return None
        return api_key

    Create an instance object and use that object as the dependency in `Depends()`.

    The dependency result will be a string containing the key value.

    ## Example

    ```python
    from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI
    from fastapi.security import APIKeyQuery

    app = FastAPI()

    query_scheme = APIKeyQuery(name="api_key")


    @app.get("/items/")
    async def read_items(api_key: str = Depends(query_scheme)):
        return {"api_key": api_key}
    ```

        self,
        *,
        name: Annotated[
            str,

class HTTPAuthorizationCredentials(BaseModel):
    """
    The HTTP authorization credentials in the result of using `HTTPBearer` or
    `HTTPDigest` in a dependency.

    The HTTP authorization header value is split by the first space.

    The first part is the `scheme`, the second part is the `credentials`.

    For example, in an HTTP Bearer token scheme, the client will send a header
    like:

    ```
    Authorization: Bearer deadbeef12346
    ```

    In this case:

    * `scheme` will have the value `"Bearer"`
    * `credentials` will have the value `"deadbeef12346"`
    """

    scheme: Annotated[
        str,
        Doc(
            """
            The HTTP authorization scheme extracted from the header value.
            """
        ),
    ]
    credentials: Annotated[
        str,
        Doc(
            """
            The HTTP authorization credentials extracted from the header value.
            """
        ),
    ]


class HTTPBase(SecurityBase):
    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        scheme: str,
        scheme_name: Optional[str] = None,
        description: Optional[str] = None,
        auto_error: bool = True,
    ):
        self.model = HTTPBaseModel(scheme=scheme, description=description)
        self.scheme_name = scheme_name or self.__class__.__name__
        self.auto_error = auto_error

    async def __call__(
        self, request: Request
    ) -> Optional[HTTPAuthorizationCredentials]:
        authorization = request.headers.get("Authorization")
        scheme, credentials = get_authorization_scheme_param(authorization)
        if not (authorization and scheme and credentials):
            if self.auto_error:
                raise HTTPException(
                    status_code=HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN, detail="Not authenticated"
                )
            else:
                return None
        return HTTPAuthorizationCredentials(scheme=scheme, credentials=credentials)

    ```python
    from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI
    from fastapi.security import HTTPBasic, HTTPBasicCredentials

    app = FastAPI()

    security = HTTPBasic()


    @app.get("/users/me")
    def read_current_user(credentials: Annotated[HTTPBasicCredentials, Depends(security)]):
        return {"username": credentials.username, "password": credentials.password}
    ```

        self,

        scheme_name: Annotated[

            Doc(

                """
            ),
        ] = None,
        realm: Annotated[
            Optional[str],

                """
                HTTP Basic authentication realm.

            status_code=HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
            detail="Invalid authentication credentials",
            headers=unauthorized_headers,

        except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError, binascii.Error):
